alerts.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 10:49PM CDT until October 17 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
...STRONG NORTHERLY WINDS FRIDAY NIGHT INCREASE WILDFIRE THREAT...

.A strong front pushes south through Deep South Texas and the Rio
Grande Valley on Friday, with a secondary surge of strong
northerly winds arriving late Friday evening into late Saturday
morning. Relative humidity values are expected to drop Friday
afternoon with little to no recovery into Saturday morning. Any
wildfire that can develop will behave dangerously with erratic
growth and spread due to strong winds and lower humidity. A Red
Flag Warning is in effect.

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Red Flag
Warning for Red Flag Warning, which is in effect from 1 PM Friday
to 7 AM CDT Saturday. The Fire Weather Watch is no longer in
effect.

* WINDS...Northerly 15-25 mph, gusting as high as 35-55 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 25 to 40 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that can develop will behave dangerously with
erratic growth and spread.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 15 at 1:48PM CDT until October 16 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest and western Texas, including the
following areas, in southwest Texas, Central Brewster, Chinati
Mountains, Chisos Basin, Davis Mountains, Davis Mountains
Foothills, Lower Brewster County, Marfa Plateau, Pecos, Presidio
Valley and Terrell. In western Texas, Andrews, Borden, Crane,
Dawson, Ector, Gaines, Glasscock, Howard, Loving, Martin, Midland,
Mitchell, Reagan, Reeves County Plains, Scurry, Upton, Ward and
Winkler.

* WHEN...Through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moisture from Hurricane Simon will stream over West Texas the
next several days. Periods of heavy rain are expected from this
system that will likely cause flash flooding, especially in urban
areas and low water crossings where drainage is poor.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 11:58PM CDT until October 17 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
alerts.description:
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS AND CENTRAL
AND SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA FRIDAY...

.Breezy and dry conditions due to a frontal passage will combine
with very dry fuels and produce red flag conditions across
portions of central and southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas
through Friday afternoon. A Fire Weather Watch is in place for
all of southeast Texas and southwest and central Louisiana on
Saturday.

...FIRE WEATHER WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM SATURDAY MORNING
THROUGH SATURDAY EVENING FOR HIGH WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY
FOR PORTIONS OF CENTRAL AND SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA AND SOUTHEAST
TEXAS...

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 027 Vernon, Fire Weather
Zone 028 Rapides, Fire Weather Zone 029 Avoyelles, Fire
Weather Zone 030 Beauregard, Fire Weather Zone 180 Tyler, Fire
Weather Zone 259 Northern Jasper and Fire Weather Zone 260
Northern Newton.

* TIMING...For the Red Flag Warning, from 11 AM Friday to 1 AM
CDT Saturday. For the Fire Weather Watch, from Saturday
morning through Saturday evening.

* WINDS...North 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 82 Friday, Up to 72 Saturday.

* LIGHTNING...

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
alerts.areaDesc: Vernon; Rapides; Avoyelles; Beauregard; Tyler; Northern Jasper; Northern Newton

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 15 at 1:01PM CDT until October 16 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS San Angelo TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of west central Texas, including the following
counties, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher,
Haskell, Irion, Jones, Nolan, Runnels, Schleicher, Shackelford,
Sterling, Sutton, Taylor, Throckmorton and Tom Green.

* WHEN...Through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is an increased danger to lives and property due to flash
flooding. Flash flooding is likely and considerable flash
flooding is possible.

- With a series of upper-level disturbances and an approaching cold
front interacting with a very moist airmass, expect focused areas
of showers and thunderstorms this afternoon and tonight. Heavy
rainfall in short periods of time will bring a risk of flooding
and flash flooding.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 15 at 1:48PM CDT until October 16 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest and western Texas, including the
following areas, in southwest Texas, Central Brewster, Chinati
Mountains, Chisos Basin, Davis Mountains, Davis Mountains
Foothills, Lower Brewster County, Marfa Plateau, Pecos, Presidio
Valley and Terrell. In western Texas, Andrews, Borden, Crane,
Dawson, Ector, Gaines, Glasscock, Howard, Loving, Martin, Midland,
Mitchell, Reagan, Reeves County Plains, Scurry, Upton, Ward and
Winkler.

* WHEN...Through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moisture from Hurricane Simon will stream over West Texas the
next several days. Periods of heavy rain are expected from this
system that will likely cause flash flooding, especially in urban
areas and low water crossings where drainage is poor.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Beaver Creek near Electra affecting Wilbarger and Wichita Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Beaver Creek near Electra.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 26.0 feet, Flood levels up to 2 feet in depth cover
farm and range lands... and may inundate some oil and gas
facilities... along and near the creek in southern Wilbarger County
and southwestern Wichita County.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:00 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 20.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 24.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 25.7 feet
Sunday evening. It will then fall below flood stage Monday
evening.
- Flood stage is 24.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 15 at 8:59PM CDT until October 18 at 10:51AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP, Texas
affecting Brewster County.

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Johnson Ranch near Castolon, Texas
affecting Brewster County.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande near Castolon, Texas affecting Brewster
County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande near Castolon,  Texas, Rio
Grande at Johnson Ranch near Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Rio
Grande Village,  BBNP,  Texas...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Johnson Ranch near Castolon,
Texas.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, minor lowland
flooding occurs, and no significant damage is expected. At 15.0
feet, flood stage is reached.  Moderate lowland flooding begins.
Roads that lead to Cottonwood Campground and River Road may flood.
Stages are practically synonymous with the gage at Cottonwood
Campground at Castolon (CSTT2), and therefore represent the reach
from Santa Elena Canyon through Cottonwood Campground, where damage
may occur.  Cattle also graze in the lowlands, and may be
threatened. At 19.0 feet, the river reaches major flood stage.
Flooding begins to occur upstream in Cottonwood Campground at
Castolon, as stages at each location are practically synonymous.
Moderate lowland flooding begins at the gage site, but no damage
occurs.  The gage is inaccessible, as River Road is impassable at
several locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 10.8 feet (3.3 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet (3.7 meters).
- Forecast...The river will fall to 6.8 feet (2.1 meters) late this
evening. It will then rise above flood stage tomorrow morning to
17.1 feet (5.2 meters) late tomorrow morning. It will fall below
flood stage early tomorrow afternoon to 12.9 feet (3.9 meters)
tomorrow evening. It will then rise above flood stage again early
Saturday morning to 17.7 feet (5.4 meters) late Saturday morning.
It will fall below flood stage again late Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet (4.6 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 18.0
feet (5.5 meters) on 07/02/2025.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 15 at 8:59PM CDT until October 18 at 6:08PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP, Texas
affecting Brewster County.

affecting Brewster County.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande near Castolon,  Texas, Rio
Grande at Johnson Ranch near Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Rio
Grande Village,  BBNP,  Texas...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande near Castolon, Texas.

* WHEN...From Friday afternoon to Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, and no
significant damage is expected. At 15.0 feet, the river reaches
minor flood stage, and lowland flooding begins.  The river begins
to flood the road between Santa Elena Canyon and Cottonwood
Campground in Big Bend National Park.  The river begins to flood
the parking lot at Santa Elena Canyon, and cut off the nature trail
into the canyon.  Campers in Cottonwood Campground need to prepare
for possible evacuations. At 19.0 feet, the river reaches moderate
flood stage, and begins flooding Cottonwood Campground.  The river
inundates the restrooms upstream at Santa Elena Canyon parking lot.
The river begins to close all area roads.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 4.9 feet (1.5 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 13.0 feet (4.0 meters).
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow afternoon to a crest of 17.5 feet (5.3 meters) late
tomorrow evening. It will then fall below flood stage Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet (4.6 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.4
feet (5.3 meters) on 10/11/2022.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 15 at 8:59PM CDT until October 19 at 9:40AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP, Texas
affecting Brewster County.

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Johnson Ranch near Castolon, Texas
affecting Brewster County.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande near Castolon, Texas affecting Brewster
County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande near Castolon,  Texas, Rio
Grande at Johnson Ranch near Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Rio
Grande Village,  BBNP,  Texas...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP,
Texas.

* WHEN...From late tonight to Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, and no damage
is expected.  Preparations may be necessary to remove water pumps.
The park should be notified at this time if additional rises are
expected so they will have time to remove the pumps. At 13.0 feet,
the river reaches minor flood stage.  Water reaches the water pumps
maintained by the park service that are used to water the
campgrounds and to provide water to the employee living quarters.
It may be necessary for park personnel to remove the pumps. At 15.0
feet, the river reaches moderate flood stage.  Water pumps
submerge. At 19.0 feet, the river reaches the bottom of telemetry
box near the pump house. At 20.0 feet, the river reaches major
flood stage.  Rio Grande Village campground begins to flood.
Evacuations may be necessary.  The rain gauge near pump house will
be affected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:00 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 1.4 feet (0.4 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet (3.7 meters).
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage late tonight to
19.4 feet (5.9 meters) early tomorrow afternoon. It will then
fall early Saturday morning. It will rise to 14.6 feet (4.5
meters) early Saturday afternoon. It will then fall below flood
stage late Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet (4.0 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 21.0
feet (6.4 meters) on 07/03/2025.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.description:
...STRONG NORTHERLY WINDS FRIDAY NIGHT INCREASE WILDFIRE THREAT...

.A strong front pushes south through Deep South Texas and the Rio
Grande Valley on Friday, with a secondary surge of strong
northerly winds arriving late Friday evening into late Saturday
morning. Relative humidity values are expected to drop Friday
afternoon with little to no recovery into Saturday morning. Any
wildfire that can develop will behave dangerously with erratic
growth and spread due to strong winds and lower humidity. A Red
Flag Warning is in effect.

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Red Flag
Warning for Red Flag Warning, which is in effect from 1 PM Friday
to 7 AM CDT Saturday. The Fire Weather Watch is no longer in
effect.

* WINDS...Northerly 15-25 mph, gusting as high as 35-55 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 25 to 40 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that can develop will behave dangerously with
erratic growth and spread.

alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6
to 9 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from Friday morning
through Sunday morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 1
PM Friday to 7 AM CDT Sunday. For the High Surf Advisory, from
1 PM Friday to 7 AM CDT Sunday.

or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations

erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is likely to occur during
high tide cycles Friday night, Saturday afternoon, and Saturday
night.

FFWEWX

The National Weather Service in Austin/San Antonio has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Val Verde County in south central Texas...

* Until 130 AM CDT.

* At 1027 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

flash flooding.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Pafford Crossing and Devils River State Nat Area Big Satan.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Foster Ranch.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 5.0 feet, Lowland flooding makes low water crossings
at Pandale on the Pecos River and tributaries flooded and
impassable. At 7.0 feet, (2.1 meters), Minor lowland flooding is a

of the Pecos River above Pandale to above Langtry. At 10.0 feet,

flood stage early Saturday afternoon to 13.3 feet Saturday
evening. It will rise above flood stage again early Sunday
morning to 16.7 feet early Sunday afternoon. It will then fall
below flood stage again late Sunday evening.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.

Saturday.

TEXAS...

alerts.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 10:49PM CDT until October 17 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
...STRONG NORTHERLY WINDS FRIDAY NIGHT INCREASE WILDFIRE THREAT...

.A strong front pushes south through Deep South Texas and the Rio
Grande Valley on Friday, with a secondary surge of strong
northerly winds arriving late Friday evening into late Saturday
morning. Relative humidity values are expected to drop Friday
afternoon with little to no recovery into Saturday morning. Any
wildfire that can develop will behave dangerously with erratic
growth and spread due to strong winds and lower humidity. A Red
Flag Warning is in effect.

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Red Flag
Warning for Red Flag Warning, which is in effect from 1 PM Friday
to 7 AM CDT Saturday. The Fire Weather Watch is no longer in
effect.

* WINDS...Northerly 15-25 mph, gusting as high as 35-55 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 25 to 40 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that can develop will behave dangerously with
erratic growth and spread.

alerts.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 15 at 11:20AM CDT until October 18 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6
to 9 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from Friday morning
through Sunday morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 1
PM Friday to 7 AM CDT Sunday. For the High Surf Advisory, from
1 PM Friday to 7 AM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is likely to occur during
high tide cycles Friday night, Saturday afternoon, and Saturday
night.

alerts.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 10:49PM CDT until October 17 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
...STRONG NORTHERLY WINDS FRIDAY NIGHT INCREASE WILDFIRE THREAT...

.A strong front pushes south through Deep South Texas and the Rio
Grande Valley on Friday, with a secondary surge of strong
northerly winds arriving late Friday evening into late Saturday
morning. Relative humidity values are expected to drop Friday
afternoon with little to no recovery into Saturday morning. Any
wildfire that can develop will behave dangerously with erratic
growth and spread due to strong winds and lower humidity. A Red
Flag Warning is in effect.

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Red Flag
Warning for Red Flag Warning, which is in effect from 1 PM Friday
to 7 AM CDT Saturday. The Fire Weather Watch is no longer in
effect.

* WINDS...Northerly 15-25 mph, gusting as high as 35-55 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 25 to 40 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that can develop will behave dangerously with
erratic growth and spread.
